title: Amoebic Liver Abscess
subject: Medicine
summary: A parasitic infection of the liver by Entamoeba histolytica presenting with RUQ pain, fever and a hypoechoic lesion. Diagnosis relies on imaging, serology and aspirate microscopy. Treatment is metronidazole plus supportive care.

sections.p: A focal collection of necrotic tissue in the liver caused by Entamoeba histolytica. Diagnosis is clinical plus imaging, serology and aspirate microscopy.

t.b: Detects a hypoechoic or anechoic lesion; confirms size and location.
Positive in >90% of cases; rules out bacterial abscess.
Shows ‘anchovy sauce’ pus; sterile culture; confirms diagnosis when serology is equivocal.
Used when ultrasound is inconclusive; shows rim‑enhancing lesion.

sections.p: Severity is graded by size, number of lesions and presence of complications such as rupture or sepsis.

sections.p: Patients have high‑grade fever, chills, right upper quadrant pain and tender hepatomegaly. Jaundice is uncommon unless the abscess ruptures into biliary tree.
Investigations focus on confirming the diagnosis and ruling out bacterial abscess.
Rupture into pleural space, peritoneum or biliary tree, sepsis, and hepatic failure are life‑threatening.
Treat with metronidazole, supportive care, and drainage if indicated.

whenToSeekHelp: Sudden worsening of pain, haemodynamic instability, new pleural effusion, jaundice, or signs of sepsis

faq.q: Why is metronidazole preferred over tinidazole?
faq.a: Metronidazole penetrates abscess cavity better and is widely available in low‑resource settings.

faq.q: Can a patient with amoebic abscess be discharged after 48 hours?
faq.a: Only if afebrile, pain controlled, and imaging shows stable lesion; otherwise continue inpatient monitoring.

faq.q: What if the patient has a penicillin allergy?
faq.a: Metronidazole is not a beta‑lactam; allergy does not affect its use.

exam: What is the first investigation you would order in a patient with RUQ pain and fever? — Ultrasound to detect a hypoechoic lesion and guide aspiration.

How would you differentiate an amoebic abscess from a pyogenic one clinically? — Amoebic abscess is usually solitary, sterile on culture, and serology positive; pyogenic is often multiloculated and culture positive.
What is the most common complication that can be life‑threatening? — Rupture into the pleural cavity causing haemothorax or into the peritoneum causing peritonitis.
Why is metronidazole chosen over clindamycin? — Metronidazole has better abscess penetration and is effective against E. histolytica; clindamycin has higher resistance and toxicity.
When is percutaneous drainage indicated? — Lesions >5 cm, multiloculated, or not responding to medical therapy after 48–72 hours.
What red flag would prompt immediate surgical consultation? — Sudden haemodynamic instability or evidence of rupture into the pleural cavity on imaging.
